transport: non-PTY stdio NDJSON; one watched pane per process

flags.--socket: Herdr Unix socket; defaults to HERDR_SOCKET_PATH
flags.--pi-agent-dir: defaults to PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR or HOME/.pi/agent; uses sessions/ and matching herdcats/<session UUID>.sock
flags.--agy-root: defaults to HOME/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain; descriptor-pinned root; no symlink traversal
flags.--cursor-root: defaults to HOME/.cursor/projects; descriptor-pinned root; no symlink traversal; transcripts are located by exact chat ID, never by project slug

capabilities.claude_timeline: true when transcript root is available; per-pane source validation still required
capabilities.codex_timeline: true when the Codex root exists; per-pane source validation still required; prompts/routed_hosts stay false
capabilities.record_content: true; rich entries and bounded content retrieval are enabled only when initialize params.record_content is true
capabilities.pi: true when the Pi sessions root is available; exact Herdr source and a verified live Pi 1.4.0 extension are required per pane
capabilities.agy: source adapter implemented; exact Herdr agent agy/antigravity_cli and source herdr:antigravity_cli required; delayed transcript creation retried
capabilities.cursor: read-only timeline adapter implemented; exact Herdr agent cursor and source herdr:cursor required; true when the adapter has a configured root; per-pane source validation still required
capabilities.cursor_prompts: true when the Cursor adapter has a configured root; the bridge, not the phone, reads the screen and submits Cursor prompts through prompt.submit

subcommands.herdcats-bridge codex-config daemon-stat: Reports running/not_running/unknown state of the managed daemon and updater, and config.toml auto_start setting; exits 0 and prints JSON
subcommands.herdcats-bridge codex-config disable-dae: Sets features.daemon_auto_start = false in Codex config.toml; with --stop-running, also safely stops the running managed daemon and updater (note: stopping disconnects sessions attached to the daemon, which must be restarted); exits 0 and prints status/error JSON whose optional daemon/updater fields are one of stopped, not_running, stop_failed, unknown (stop_failed = still running after the stop passes — including a process that started or restarted mid-operation — or any stop command failed, exited nonzero, or timed out; unknown = a possibly-matching process is alive but its identity could not be verified; it is never signalled)

params.record_content: optional bool; false by default for older clients
params.approvals: optional bool; false by default; opts into approval interaction events and responses
params.questions: optional bool; false by default; independently opts into question interaction events and responses
params.model_control: optional bool; false by default; opts into model.status/model.set requests and model.updated events

requests.effect: clears watch; validates Herdr protocol22; required before other methods

params.before: stable first entry ID from preceding page

requests.effect: revalidates source before serving; may emit notifications before response

params.content_ref: opaque source reference published on an entry

requests.effect: Revalidates native occupant and source; returns at most64KiB raw bytes encoded as lowercase hex. Only current retained entry references are readable; no host paths accepted.

params.request_id: string from the last interaction.pending event
params.option: one-based u32 option number, not the zero-based selected index
params.label_lines: array of strings copied exactly from that option; preserve row boundaries and order

result_types.sent: string; exactly one Claude digit shortcut, Codex letter shortcut, or esc; never Enter
result_types.confirmed: boolean; true when the visible screen no longer parses as the same dialog; false if it remains or confirmation reads fail

requests.requires: initialize with params.approvals true for approvals or params.questions true for questions, and a watch with a resolved native identity
validation: The request_id must equal the last emitted pending approval for the current watch identity and generation.
Re-read the visible screen and parse with the same hook command; dialog content and option keys must match the emitted dialog. A highlight-only change is allowed.
The option number must exist and its complete label_lines array must equal the echoed rows.

Re-read the spool and adapter-verified transcript/rollout, bypassing the polling match cache. The same call must still be Pending and the newest pending request in the session, with unchanged tool name, input and Codex turn attribution.
A fresh Herdr snapshot must still show the same native occupant blocked in the same pane and terminal.

errors.unsupported_capability: Client did not opt in to the corresponding approvals or questions capability.
errors.timeline_unavailable: The watch has no resolved identity or its timeline is unavailable.
errors.stale: No matching emitted request, changed/unreadable dialog or source, resolved/aborted or superseded call, or changed/unblocked/missing pane. Preflight and approval errors send no input. During question execution, includes steps_sent: number of input steps dispatched, conservatively counting a failed send whose delivery may be uncertain.
errors.mismatch: The option number is invalid or its label_lines differ from the exact rows shown. No keys are sent. For questions, answers do not fit the request.
errors.in_progress: Question screen is no longer fresh; no input sent.
errors.invalid: Invalid answer indices, cardinality, option numbers or text.

requests.effect: After validation, send exactly one shortcut without Enter. Re-read the visible screen for up to about 2 seconds with short waits. Return confirmed: false rather than an error if the key was sent but disappearance could not be confirmed; do not automatically resend. Write the result, then poll so interaction.resolved can follow promptly.

question_params.answers: array of {index: zero-based question index, options: [one-based option number], text?: string}; answer every question exactly once; omit for skip
question_params.skip: true only for Codex async; omit answers

question_validation: Each answer requires at least one option or non-empty text, including multi-select: submitting a multi-select with nothing chosen is not supported (unverified terminal behaviour), so answer it in Terminal. Single-select accepts at most one option; multi-select accepts several. Option numbers exclude the free-text row. Codex Plan requires exactly one option, including None of the above for a text-only answer.
Text is a single line of at most 500 characters with no control characters.

Respond only from a fresh screen. Recheck the pending request, identity, blocked status and fresh visible screen before sending; verify the expected next screen between steps. Stop on mismatch with stale and steps_sent.
requests.question_result: request_id and confirmed: boolean; true when the dialog is observed gone after the final input (or after the last Codex Plan digit). False if final confirmation fails or the unchanged final dialog remains for about 1 second. Never resend automatically.
requests.question_effect: Revalidate the newest pending request without the polling cache, identity, occupant, blocked status and fresh visible screen before input. Execute the pure key/text plan, polling the visible screen every 100ms for at most about 1 second after each step. Re-read before later inputs and revalidate the occupant before sending. Stop with stale and steps_sent on an unexpected state or intermediate read/send failure. Send the optional final Codex Plan Enter only if the selected last picker is still visible; skip it if the dialog has gone. Write the result, then poll so interaction.resolved can follow.

result_types.agent: claude, codex, antigravity_cli, pi or cursor
result_types.model: {id, label} or null; the model in effect from the transcript (Claude assistant message.model + effort, Codex idle/done catalog-matched live footer, otherwise last turn_context), falling back to Claude settings.json or Codex config.toml when no turns exist yet; Agy exposes the normalized family ID/base label and discovered efforts from its verified live footer (base · effort or an exact native catalog label carrying a recognized effort suffix)
result_types.effort: reasoning effort id (low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra, minimal) or null
result_types.models: selectable {id, label, efforts: [{id, label}], current?: bool} models, each with its own effort options (empty when none): Claude tier aliases (fable, opus, sonnet, haiku) plus the live current id when unmapped; Codex catalog slugs from models_cache.json filtered to visibility=list and ordered by priority; exactly one entry carries current=true when a model is known; Agy groups matching terminal -low/-medium/-high IDs and (Low)/(Medium)/(High) labels into base family IDs/labels with discovered efforts. Unknown or ambiguous native rows remain lossless
result_types.efforts: effort options for the current model: Claude low/medium/high/xhigh/max (auto hidden); Codex per-model supported_reasoning_levels, or the standard set when the model is unknown; empty when none

requests.requires: initialize with params.model_control true and a watch with a resolved native identity

errors.unsupported_capability: Client did not opt in to model control.
errors.timeline_unavailable: The watch has no resolved identity or its timeline is unavailable.
errors.stale: The pane or occupant changed or the transcript could not be re-verified.
errors.unsupported_agent: The watched agent has no supported model adapter.

requests.effect: Runs a poll first (emitting any pending timeline events), then reads the current model/effort and option lists. Read-only: never sends input.

params.text: required non-empty string, at most 65536 bytes, no NUL; a message whose first non-space character is / is refused with slash_command_refused because Cursor would run it as a command
params.expect: required {identity, generation} from the latest snapshot; otherwise stale

requests.requires: initialize, then a watch with a resolved Cursor identity. Cursor only; other agents get unsupported_agent. Advertised by capabilities.cursor_prompts.
validation: The pane must still be the same terminal, agent and chat, with Herdr status idle or done; otherwise agent_busy or stale.

The visible screen must show Cursor's idle composer with its faint placeholder and nothing else: no permission card, skip-feedback input, question form, picker or typed text. Herdr's status is not trusted because a live AskQuestion form is reported as done and Cursor writes no pending card to its transcript.

Refusal codes: approval_pending, question_pending, composer_not_empty, agent_busy, picker_open, screen_unrecognized, screen_unavailable, slash_command_refused, invalid_request, stale, unsupported_agent.
The guard and the Herdr agent.prompt call are one bridge call. A failed send is prompt_unconfirmed and is never retried; a transport error may still have delivered it.

params.model: optional model id or Claude alias to switch to; omit to keep; Agy accepts normalized family IDs or exact discovered native IDs for legacy clients
params.effort: optional effort id to switch to; omit to keep
params.expect: required {model: id|null, effort: id|null}; the client's last observed pair from model.status or model.updated; Agy also requires identity and generation. A family expectation is accepted only with the exact effort of the authoritative native pair

result_types.applied: {model: {id, label}|null, effort: id|null}; the pair in effect after the attempt: the confirmed new values for steps that succeeded, the prior values otherwise
result_types.confirmed: boolean; true when every requested step was confirmed on screen
result_types.error: null on success; unknown_model, invalid_effort, stale, composer_not_empty, picker_mismatch, change_declined or confirm_timeout when a sent command failed its screen confirmation (partial results still return applied)

requests.requires: initialize with params.model_control true and a watch with a resolved native identity
validation: The agent status must be idle or done; working and blocked panes are refused with agent_busy before any input.
A fresh Herdr snapshot and adapter re-resolution must still show the same pane, terminal, agent and native session; otherwise stale.
The transcript scan must equal the expect pair exactly; otherwise stale (the desk changed it).

Claude sends /model first, waits for the Set model to confirmation (its text supplies the applied label), then /effort and its confirmation; an invalid model stops the flow, an invalid effort still reports the applied model.

Claude may show a Switch model? or Change effort level? cache-switch dialog. The bridge verifies both numbered options and the requested target (case-insensitive model-label prefix or exact effort), rechecks occupant/idle status and the visible dialog, then sends digit 1 once. A mismatched target returns picker_mismatch. A timeout or mismatch sends digit 2 only while a fresh read still shows the recognizable dialog with No, go back. The Set confirmation must differ from the pre-send baseline and follow the submitted command; Kept model/effort results fail with change_declined.

Before every agent.prompt, the visible composer must be provably empty or the request returns composer_not_empty without sending input. Occupant and idle/done status are rechecked before subsequent sends; a mid-flow change returns stale (with Claude partial applied values) and dismisses an open Codex picker.

Codex submits /model through Herdr's agent.prompt, then drives the picker with arrows and verifies the screen, model label, row labels and cursor before enter or s; enter on the model list only advances to the effort step, including lists with ten or more models; max/ultra open the nested Advanced Reasoning entry first. The effort is applied with the s session-only key, never the digit/enter default-persist paths, so config.toml is not written.

errors.unsupported_capability: Client did not opt in to model control.
errors.timeline_unavailable: The watch has no resolved identity or its timeline is unavailable.
errors.invalid_request: Missing expect object, or an empty/oversized model id.
errors.invalid_effort: Effort id outside the agent's known set; no input sent.
errors.agent_busy: Pane status is working or blocked; no input sent.
errors.stale: Occupant/status changed or the expect pair disagrees with the transcript; no further apply input is sent. An open Codex picker is dismissed.
errors.composer_not_empty: The composer contains a draft or could not be proven empty; no prompt is sent (Claude may return a previously applied model as a partial result).
errors.change_declined: Claude kept the prior model or effort; applied retains the previously confirmed pair.
errors.picker_mismatch: A Claude cache-switch dialog did not match the requested target (declined only while visible), or a Codex picker screen did not show the expected title/rows; the picker is dismissed with Escape.
errors.confirm_timeout: The command or picker never confirmed within about 4 seconds; the Codex picker is dismissed with Escape.

requests.effect: Applies from the next turn in the session. Claude writes the CLI's own persisted defaults (settings.json); Codex applies for this session only and writes nothing. Confirmed and partially applied pairs override the unchanged scan for model.status, subsequent expect checks and model.updated. The override is discarded when the scanned pair changes or the identity/generation resets. Agy keeps scans, overrides and confirmations native and normalizes only wire results. Family switches preserve current effort if discovered, otherwise prefer medium, low, then high. Explicit legacy native targets retain their concrete selection; effort-only requests resolve a discovered variant of the current family. No native ID is invented for submission.

failure.id: request ID or null for invalid frame/ID

error.steps_sent: optional integer on question execution stale errors; key lists and text inputs each count as one step

client_scope: Also bind to SSH host, Herdr session and local connection generation; those are not emitted by this helper.

timeline.snapshot.effect: replace state; recent page only; fetch earlier retained entries separately With model_control opted in and a verified Agy footer, optional model and effort fields carry the normalized current family, matching model.status and model.updated.

timeline.updated.effect: Remove evicted_ids before stable-ID upserts; retention does not reset generation. Do not resurrect evicted IDs from delayed history. Counters may update with no entries; frames remain bounded.

timeline.unavailable.effect: clear selected timeline and invalidate cursors. For Codex panes with session_reference_unavailable, ambiguous_session or invalid_session_reference, data carries codex_daemon ('running' | 'not_running' | 'unknown'). Stopping the daemon disconnects active sessions attached to it, which must be restarted.

field_types.identity: object with pane_id, terminal_id, agent and native_session_id; same identity as the watched timeline
field_types.generation: u64; timeline generation for this approval
field_types.request_id: string; Claude tool_use_id or Codex rollout call_id; uncorrelated hook records produce no event
field_types.tool_name: string from the hook, for example Bash
field_types.description: string from Claude hook tool_input.description, verbatim, or null; null for Codex
field_types.justification: string from the Codex hook justification (tool_input.description), verbatim, or null; null for Claude
field_types.environment: string parsed from the visible screen, or null
field_types.title: string parsed from the visible screen
field_types.options: array of option objects, in visible screen order
field_types.selected: zero-based index into options, or null when no highlight is visible

option_fields.number: one-based u32 displayed option number; echo as interaction.respond params.option
option_fields.label_lines: array of visible label rows, preserving row boundaries; never join rows when echoing a response
option_fields.key: string parsed from the screen: Claude digit shortcut, Codex letter shortcut, or esc; the client echoes number and label_lines, not a key

interaction.pending.effect: Show only the newest correlated Pending request when the pane is blocked and exactly one visible dialog matches its hook command. Emit only on a changed request, dialog content/keys, or selection (and after identity/generation reset). A replacement request emits interaction.resolved for the old request first.

question_fields.request_id: Claude ask-<payload.prompt_id>-<record t in whole milliseconds> from the hook spool, or Codex call_id
question_fields.questions: array of {index: zero-based integer, header: string|null, text: string, options: [{number: one-based integer, label: string, description: string|null}], multi_select: boolean, allows_other: boolean}; free-text row excluded from options
question_fields.step: object: {kind: claude_question, index}, {kind: claude_review}, {kind: codex_question, index, total}, {kind: async_queued}, or {kind: async_picker, index}; indices are zero-based
question_fields.fresh: boolean; untouched first Claude tab with cursor on option 1 and no checks/text or completed tabs; Codex Plan Question 1/n with n unanswered and no notes; async queued or picker cursor on 1 without text

interaction.pending.question_effect: Enabled only by initialize params.questions true. Match newest pending Claude question from its recording hook spool plus answered transcript calls, or Codex question from the rollout alone, while blocked; cache Claude by spool and transcript stamps and Codex by rollout stamp, re-read visible screen each poll. Suppress secret questions, multi-question async requests, async requests when more than one async call is pending in the session, async queued banners whose count is not exactly 1, and screens that do not parse. Approvals take priority. Emit on changed step or fresh state (also countdown/payload changes).

question_client_limits.agy_behavior: Enforced before advertising a pending card. Oversized or unsupported native requests remain in history with Terminal fallback; unresolved native calls still block composition and model changes. Fenced terminal-history examples never authorize a question response or count as a second live picker.

approval_client_limits.agy_behavior: Agy has exactly four sequential choices with navigate keys and a verified selected index. Bounds are enforced before advertising. The 1024-byte bound applies to each displayed label line, not the joined scope label. Unsupported cards retain history/Terminal fallback, and unresolved native calls continue to block compose/model controls.

field_types.identity: object; identity of the previously emitted interaction, including on occupant replacement
field_types.generation: u64; generation of the previously emitted interaction
field_types.request_id: string; previously emitted request ID: Claude approval tool_use_id, Claude question ask-<prompt_id>-<milliseconds>, or Codex rollout call_id

interaction.resolved.effect: Clear the matching pending interaction once when the call resolves/aborts, the pane leaves blocked, the dialog disappears or becomes uncertain, or the identity changes. initialize and unwatch reset pending state without emitting this event. Same-identity source_changing retries preserve the existing interaction without emitting interaction.resolved.

field_types.model: {id, label}; the label is the CLI-confirmed one while an override holds, otherwise the Codex catalog display name or the derived Claude label; Agy exposes the normalized family ID/base label and discovered efforts
field_types.effort: string or null; the effort observed in the transcript

model.updated.effect: Emitted only when initialize opted into model control, after a transcript or live Codex idle-footer scan observes a different model/effort pair (and once after an identity/generation reset). Claude confirmed labels remain authoritative while the watch override holds. Codex session-only changes survive reconnects through the catalog-matched idle/done footer; missing or unparseable footers fall back to transcript/config. Pairs with model.set results: the request's applied pair is authoritative until the transcript catches up.

entry_fields.id: message:<source UUID>, tool:<tool ID>, or content:<source byte offset>:<block index>
entry_fields.kind: message/tool; image/record when record_content is negotiated
entry_fields.truncated: boolean, conservatively preserved for replayed tools
entry_fields.content_ref: optional opaque reference to complete block bytes
entry_fields.record_refs: optional references to complete original record bytes; up to4 per entry

reconnect: No persistent replay cursor. Start a new helper, initialize and watch. Epoch change or sequence gap requires fresh snapshot. Notifications can interleave all replies.
cursor: Generation-bound before entry ID. Identity/source replacement or genuine outage recovery resets generation. Normal retention keeps generation; a retained cursor remains valid and an evicted cursor returns stale_cursor.

limits.oversized_source_record_behavior: Complete source lines exceeding the parsed record limit use bounded typed deserialization for text/tools. Negotiated rich mode additionally emits image descriptors and unfamiliar-record bubbles with complete source references, without embedding bulky image bytes in live frames. Incomplete lines wait for newline; the 64MiB source bound remains hard.

source_policy: Herdr22 references use herdr:claude or herdr:codex. Claude native UUID filenames/paths stay beneath the pinned transcript root; Codex rollouts stay beneath the pinned sessions root and verify session metadata and pane cwd. Ambiguous references, symlinks below pinned roots, missing references or foreign main-session records fail closed.
implementation_limits: Bounded source prefix reread on change, new complete records parsed incrementally.
Negotiated content retrieval covers complete original records and blocks within the verified 64MiB source; only references on retained entries are readable.
Claude captured2.1.296 schema coverage; no general version promise.

Optional four-platform installer and native iOS client. Bridge approval and question events and guarded responses are available from 0.3.0 for Claude and Codex. Clients must gate on the approvals / questions capabilities and corresponding initialize opt-ins, not on bridge_version. Claude cards require the recording hook (herdcats-bridge hooks install --agent claude); Codex approval cards require the Codex recording hook (herdcats-bridge hooks install --agent codex), while Codex question cards require no recording hook. prompts and routed_hosts (saved-machine routing) remain unavailable.
transient_read_behavior: source_changing retries without clearing verified cache for the same identity; after repeated retries (threshold 10), emits timeline.updated with delayed: true while keeping verified history until recovery clears it. A changed occupant still clears old state.

approval_policy.data_sources: Options come from the visible screen; command/description come from the hook. Codex justification also comes from the hook. Keep command, description and justification verbatim; preserve option label_lines as separate rows.
approval_policy.dialog_notices: Between the Claude command border and approval prompt, accept only blank rows or exact known notices after trimming whitespace (currently: This command requires approval). Retain notice rows in dialog identity so notice changes invalidate a response; they do not replace the hook description or justification.
approval_policy.authority: The terminal dialog stays in charge. The bridge mirrors it and answers only with guarded shortcuts; it never sends Enter.
approval_policy.eligibility: Require all three: a spool record correlated to a still-pending native call, Herdr agent_status blocked, and exactly one dialog parsed from source visible anchored to the hook command. Never use scrollback/recent text or guess an uncorrelated request.
approval_policy.bounds: Keep every pending frame below wire_frame_bytes. Suppress an oversized approval instead of truncating command, metadata or labels.
approval_policy.input_failures: Approval spool/screen/tail read failures yield no card and do not themselves emit timeline.unavailable. Same-identity timeline source_changing retries preserve an already emitted card until verification can resume.
approval_policy.capability: Approval and question support for Claude and Codex is available from 0.3.0. Clients must gate on the approvals / questions capabilities and corresponding initialize opt-ins, not on bridge_version. approvals: true advertises bridge support; initialize params.approvals must be true to enable approval interaction events, responses and reads. questions: true requires a separate initialize params.questions opt-in. Claude cards require the recording hook (herdcats-bridge hooks install --agent claude); Codex approval cards require the Codex recording hook (herdcats-bridge hooks install --agent codex), while Codex question cards require no recording hook. Cards still require verified live inputs; prompts and routed_hosts remain false and unavailable.

question_policy.sources: Claude question cards, available from 0.3.0, require the recording PermissionRequest hook installed (herdcats-bridge hooks install --agent claude): pending AskUserQuestion requests come from its session spool, since the transcript writes the call only after answering or Esc cancel. Pair identical inputs one-to-one against answered transcript tool calls in timestamp order, requiring a valid call timestamp no more than 2 seconds after or 120 seconds before its spool record. Missing spool means no Claude question card. Codex question cards use the rollout alone and require no recording hook. Read only for blocked panes.
question_policy.eligibility: Newest pending request, no secrets, exactly one question and exactly one pending async call for Codex async, a queued banner count of exactly 1 if queued, and exactly one parsed visible question screen. Approval cards take priority.
question_policy.resolution: Resolve when request is no longer pending, pane leaves blocked, screen no longer parses, or identity changes. Same-identity source_changing preserves pending state. initialize/unwatch silently reset.
question_policy.bounds: Suppress oversized events rather than truncating question text or options.

agy.identity: canonical antigravity_cli; native id only; never cwd/newest discovery
agy.interactions: verified Agy 1.4.7 command permission card only; once/conversation/persistent/deny; guarded arrows and Enter. Unsupported file/URL/MCP cards use Terminal. Questions decode args.questions JSON string; planner DONE remains pending until GENERIC result; only unambiguous single-call batches. Each input rechecks identity/source/screen. No uncertain send retries.
agy.model_control: agy --version and bounded agy models catalog; only tested 1.4.7; idle empty composer; exact slash command; fresh acknowledgement plus footer. /model may persist across sessions. expect.identity and expect.generation required for model.set.
agy.limits: 64 MiB source, 1 MiB record, 1000 retained entries, 8192-byte previews, 64 KiB content chunks. Rewrite/rotation reset generation and invalidate pending actions.
agy.distribution: source support only; app published installer remains 0.3.0. Publish and verify real artifact/checksum before changing app release pin.

pi.identity: exact herdr:pi session path/header, pane and terminal; native_instance_id pins the live extension runtime; never cwd/newest discovery
pi.source: existing Pi 1.4.0 TUI with the opt-in Herdcats extension; native branch entries and streaming updates over a same-user Unix socket
pi.model_control: model.status and model.set use provider/model IDs and thinking levels from the extension catalog; expect.identity, generation, model and effort are required. Confirmed or validated legacy applied replies are projected into the standard model result envelope.
pi.actions: pi.prompt (text), pi.cancel, pi.dialog.respond (request_id and value) require pane_id and expect.identity/generation; the bridge binds them to the live instance and revision. Confirmation returns confirmed:true; actions are never automatically resent.
pi.dialogs: pi.dialog carries identity, generation, request_id, kind, title, message and dialog_options. confirm returns boolean, select returns the exact option, input returns text; custom/editor dialogs remain terminal-only. pi.dialog.cleared retires the matching request_id.
pi.limits: 1 MiB extension frames; last 2000 native branch records; 1000 projected entries; 8192-byte previews. Oversized state remains terminal-only.
pi.distribution: source bridge and opt-in extension installation; published app installer pin remains unchanged. See ios/docs/pi-conversations.md and bridge/pi-extension/README.md.

cursor_cli.identity: canonical cursor; Herdr agent_session {agent: cursor, source: herdr:cursor, kind: id, value: chat UUID} only. The transcript is found by a bounded listing of every project directory and must match exactly one; the project slug (lossy, hashed when long), cwd and mtime are never used. Two matches are ambiguous_session. A missing file is retried as delayed creation.
cursor_cli.identity_limits: Herdr reports the session at launch, but not after `cursor-agent --resume` (no agent_session: session_reference_unavailable, Terminal fallback) and not after `/new` (the old chat ID stays bound, so the timeline keeps showing the previous chat). The second case cannot be detected from Herdr data and is not guessed around.
cursor_cli.records: user (outer <timestamp>/<user_query> envelope stripped when complete, otherwise verbatim), assistant text and tool_use blocks. There is no tool_result, no tool-call ID and no thinking block. Entry IDs are cursor:<byte offset>:message|tool:<n>. A tool entry is written only after its approval or question resolved and is marked completed meaning recorded, never succeeded or approved.
cursor_cli.turn_ended: The trailing {type: turn_ended} line is overwritten in place by the next prompt. It is never consumed or turned into an entry; the follower rewinds to its start. An unparsable final line (a torn overwrite) is held back the same way. Both leave the generation unchanged. Edits to the consumed prefix, a shrink below it or a rotation reset the generation.
cursor_cli.interactions: Shell permission cards only, read from the screen (Cursor writes nothing to the transcript while a call is pending). The card must be the last thing on screen with a single-row command, the allowlist notice (`Shell allowlist is empty`, or `Not in allowlist: a, b` when the user's allow list is non-empty, whose names must match the Add Shell(...) button as a set) and exactly four rows: Run (once), Add Shell(...) to allowlist?, Run Everything and Skip & tell the agent. Wrapped commands, other notices, other tools (file, MCP, fetch, plan) and any variation stay in Terminal. Only Run (once) and Skip are advertised, with their screen numbers 1 and 4 and exact labels; the allowlist and Run Everything rows persist permissions or change the whole session and stay in Terminal. Responses are guarded arrow keys then Enter, rechecking identity, transcript prefix and the exact card before every key. Skip also submits the empty 'tell the agent what to do instead' input. Model and effort control is described under model_control.
cursor_cli.confirmation_design: For later sections: the transcript has no tool_result and writes a call only after resolution, so a pending card is known only from the screen and a response is confirmed only by the card disappearing from the screen plus the matching tool_use being appended. That is a weaker guarantee than Agy's result records: it shows the call was recorded, not whether it ran or was denied, and answers to questions are not recorded at all.
cursor_cli.limits: 64 MiB source, 1 MiB record, 128 tool calls per record, 10000 project directories, 1000 retained entries, 8192-byte previews, 64 KiB content chunks.
cursor_cli.distribution: source support only; app published installer remains 0.3.0.
cursor_cli.request_id: cursor:<transcript byte length>:<FNV-1a of the command>. The length changes whenever a resolved call is appended, so an identical retried command gets a new ID.
cursor_cli.prompts: prompt.submit (see requests). Phone prompts never go through the Herdr CLI path for Cursor panes.
cursor_cli.confirmation: Confirmed means: the card left the screen (and was not the skip-feedback input) and a Shell tool_use with exactly that command was appended at or after the request's byte offset, within 5 seconds. The transcript has no result, so this proves only that the call was recorded after resolution; it cannot distinguish run from denied, and a long-running command is recorded late and returns confirmed false while the screen has already moved on.
cursor_cli.questions: AskQuestion forms (the boxed `Question i of N` screen), read from the screen: Cursor appends the call to the transcript only after the form is answered, and Herdr reports a live form as done. A form is advertised only when the box is the last thing on screen with the known hint, a cursor row, a trailing `Other: (type to answer)` write-in row, at most 8 questions and 32 options. The form shows one question at a time, so each visible question is its own request (question_kind cursor, step {kind: cursor_question, index, total}, request_id cursor-q:<transcript length>:<n>of<total>:<digest of title, prompt, multi flag and labels>) and the next arrives as a new request after Enter. fresh is true only for an untouched question (cursor on row 1, nothing checked, write-in empty); otherwise respond returns in_progress. While a form is pending the reported agent_status is blocked. Answers use guarded Down/Up, Space (a radio for single-select, a toggle for multi-select) and typing on the write-in row, then Enter; every key rechecks identity, transcript prefix and the exact form. Single-select takes one option or a write-in, multi-select any options plus a write-in; write-in is one line of at most 500 characters. skip is not supported: Esc discards the whole form at the desk, so it stays in Terminal. Confirmation: after Enter the next question is showing, or for the last question the form closed and an AskQuestion call asking that prompt was appended within 5 seconds. Neither shows what was chosen, and the transcript never records the answers.
cursor_cli.model_control: model.status and model.set work for Cursor only on the exact verified build, 2026.10.22-27dcf5f. The version is read from the live session each time (the foreground process's .../cursor-agent/versions/<version>/index.js via Herdr pane.process_info), never only from `cursor-agent --version` or the symlink, because the installed build can be replaced by an auto-update while an older session keeps running. A different version, several versions or none is refused with cursor_unsupported_version or cursor_version_unverified before any input; the cached catalog is per version. Both calls require Herdr status idle or done AND a screen showing the idle, empty composer in the default Agent mode (no Plan/Ask/Debug label, no draft, no approval card, question form or open menu); otherwise agent_busy, composer_not_empty, mode_not_agent, approval_pending, question_pending or picker_open, with no input sent. The catalog is the picker's own rows, not `cursor-agent --list-models`: those flat ids do not match what `/model <id>` accepts (a typed id is a fuzzy filter; `claude-opus-5` selected Claude Opus 5.5 and 17 of 57 derived family ids are not in the picker). Ids on the wire are slugs of the picker label (Claude Opus 5.5 -> claude-opus-5-5) and are never typed into the terminal. The catalog is read once per version by opening `/model`, walking the list with verified Down then Up steps, and closing with Esc (about 4 seconds for 46 rows). A model is chosen by typing its exact label into the picker filter one character per key (the picker ignores pasted text), moving to the row whose label matches exactly, and pressing Enter; success needs an idle composer whose footer names that label. Effort is changed in the parameter editor: Tab on the model's row, Down/Up to the radio under `Effort` or `Reasoning`, Enter, then Esc. Effort ids are low, medium, high, xhigh (Extra High), max, none, minimal, ultra from the editor's own labels; a model without such a group offers none. Efforts of a model are read from its editor when it is the current model or right after it was selected; other models list none until then. Context size, Fast and Thinking are not controlled and keep their values. Every picker step is verified on screen, a key is sent only after re-reading the screen it must act on, the picker opens only once it is stable and its cursor row agrees with the live footer (its first frame is drawn at the top of the list and keys sent into it are lost), nothing is retried, and every path ends by closing the picker or editor with Esc and requiring the idle composer again; if that fails the error is picker_stuck. Other codes: footer_unrecognized (a custom statusline hides the model), unknown_model, invalid_effort, picker_mismatch, picker_unavailable, catalog_incomplete, catalog_ambiguous, confirm_timeout, stale (expect.model, expect.effort, expect.identity or expect.generation differ). expect.identity and expect.generation are required, as for Agy. PERSISTENCE: Cursor itself writes every model or effort change to its cli-config.json (model, selectedModel and modelParameters), so a change made here also becomes the user's default for future Cursor sessions on that computer, not just this one. The app says so in the Configure sheet. The bridge never reads or writes that file. FOOTER AND CUSTOM STATUSLINES: the model in use is read from the footer under the composer, which a user's `statusLine` command replaces. A statusline is supported only when its first row starts with the exact picker label followed by a space or the end of the text (the longest such label wins, so `Claude Opus 5 ...` is never read as `Claude Opus 5.5`); everything after the recognized parameter words (context size, an effort word, Fast, Thinking, `max`) is ignored, which covers the context bar, usage and directory segments, a second wrapped row and a `· branch` suffix. Probed with a copy of the user's real ~/.cursor/statusline.sh, which prints `display_name` (already containing the parameters), then `param_summary` (repeating them), then a bar, a monthly figure and the directory; its footer is two rows when it wraps. The effort is taken only when the distinct effort words agree. A statusline that prints another name, a lowercase or abbreviated name, a partial name or nothing is refused with footer_unrecognized before any input, and so is a change request whose expect pair no longer matches. A statusline refreshes about once a second, so after an effort change the footer is waited for up to 4 seconds rather than read once (a single read produced a false confirm_timeout on the real setup). The footer is the statusline's own text: a script that prints the wrong model name would be believed, so every model and effort change is additionally checked against the picker cursor row and the editor's selected radio.
